question.problem: An arithmetic series has ${a}_{2}=5$ and ${a}_{9}=19,$ where ${a}_{2}$ and ${a}_{9}$ are the second and ninth terms of the series, respectively. What is the sum of the first $12$ terms of the series, expressed using sigma notation?
question.worked_solution:
Since we know two terms of the arithmetic series, we can find its common difference:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\frac{{a}_{9}-{a}_{2}}{9-2} \\  & =\frac{19-5}{9-2} \\  & =\frac{14}{7} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

As ${a}_{2}=5$, using the formula for the $n$th term, we can compute ${a}_{1}$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\ 5 & ={a}_{1}+(2-1)(2) \\ 5 & ={a}_{1}+2 \\ {a}_{1} & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So we have ${a}_{1}=3$ and $d=2.$ Thus, the formula for the $n$th term is:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =3+(n-1)(2) \\  & =3+2n-2 \\  & =2n+1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the sum of the first $12$ terms can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{12}(2n+1)\end{aligned}
$$
